title: The Token Still Passes, Explained
subtitle: Verity Marris, Anneke Tolan and Casimir Beng on timing twelve teams' stand-ups to see whether a speaking token has evened out the floor
summary: A research explainer from the School of Emergent Priorities on Verity Marris, Anneke Tolan and Casimir Beng's audit of the speaking token passed at the daily stand-ups of twelve open-plan teams. It follows the stopwatch through 342 stand-ups, sets the floor time measured beside the fairness the teams report, and asks what the token is still for. Tolan, Marris and Beng describe the work in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the paper auditing a hand-held speaking token at the daily stand-ups of twelve open-plan teams, which finds floor-time equality no better after four years of passing it, felt fairness running ahead of measured equality, and most attendees unable to say what the token was for

beats.tagline: A Speaking-Time Audit of a Workshop-Born Turn-Taking Ritual
beats.byline: Verity Marris, Anneke Tolan and Casimir Beng, Schools of Emergent Priorities and Continuous Improvement

beats.text: Twelve teams on the same floor now run some version of the practice, in tenures ranging from one to four years, and none has formally revisited whether the mechanism does what its adopters believe it does.
